source.title: Defiant: recover Thursday defiant-os Nipsey sourcing, catalog matching and clipping workflow
source.body:
## Product direction and outcome

Recover the **Nipsey source-discovery → review → catalog pairing → clip → campaign** workflow from Thursday October 15's AI Studio/imported Docker prototype. The owner reports that it worked for the intended use case and wants that experience brought into Defiant. The current cultural opportunity graph does not replace this source/video operations workflow. Use the earlier experience as the functional baseline, adapting implementation where necessary; do not rebuild a generic dashboard or spend the first delivery on unrelated platform infrastructure.

Repository identified: [ChaiWithJai/defiant-os](https://github.com/ChaiWithJai/defiant-os), pinned main `5e6b5c3542e9b2bd3d74080fda649abc650b80ec`. Initial import `10d1d406e53b6efae2dc259d58ae36cff01cadac` at 2026-10-15 22:44 UTC, container checks `8b8b695`, followed by introduction/identity documentation through `5e6b5c3`. The code matches the owner's date, Docker setup and Nipsey use case; AI Studio authorship/session provenance is owner-reported, not independently recoverable from this Git history.

Related delivered work: #209/#211/#214 and #218–#220 (Defiant organization, graph, shared notes/views, reports and explicit existing-editor handoff). Those closures describe the approved manual first slice, not delivery of the Thursday prototype's complete workflow.

## Inventory of the reference application

| Surface/artifact | What it contains / does |
| --- | --- |
| [Campaign interface](https://github.com/ChaiWithJai/defiant-os/blob/5e6b5c3542e9b2bd3d74080fda649abc650b80ec/public/index.html) | Five task tabs: Campaign Workstreams, Creator Videos Inbox, Paid Video Boosts, Create a 9:16 Short, Music Catalog & Royalties. Dark visual treatment, portfolio cards, searchable/filterable video table, track selector, phone video preview, workbook download and local action feedback. |
| Creator inbox | Title/creator/song search, stage and workstream filters; video links, views, likes/comments/like rate, narrative hook, matched track and action to open in studio. This searches existing records, not YouTube. |
| Workstream | Name, target song, creator bounty, budget and creative instructions; creates a persisted local workstream. Four initial themes: PROLIFIC press run; estate/ownership; street/lyric lore; Marathon Burger/lifestyle. Retain owner intent but review sensational/unsupported assertions before use. |
| Clip setup | Source video + catalog track + headline + 8/10/12-second selection + -14/-18/-22dB music setting, generated MP4 preview. |
| Paid planning | Source/platform/track/budget form, local simulated ad record and computed example impressions/clicks/streams/ROAS. No provider delivery. |
| [SQLite model](https://github.com/ChaiWithJai/defiant-os/blob/5e6b5c3542e9b2bd3d74080fda649abc650b80ec/database.py) | Five tables: catalog_tracks, clipping_campaigns, ugc_videos, bofu_ad_campaigns, rendered_clips. 45 seeded video records, 12 catalog rows, four workstreams and **five** initial paid rows (README/UI mention six in places). Rank is video identity; no observation history or source import service. |
| [HTTP service](https://github.com/ChaiWithJai/defiant-os/blob/5e6b5c3542e9b2bd3d74080fda649abc650b80ec/server.py) | Python standard-library ThreadingHTTPServer, GET health/dashboard/workbook/renders; POST workstreams, stage updates, render and local paid planning. Dashboard is SQLite aggregation. No authentication/org scoping. |
| [Renderer/reference AI](https://github.com/ChaiWithJai/defiant-os/blob/5e6b5c3542e9b2bd3d74080fda649abc650b80ec/clipper_engine.py) | Working FFmpeg command path for generated background/text/waveform and synthesized tones, voice-like envelope and timed music swell; H.264/AAC 540×960, duration clamped 5–15 sec. Does **not** read the selected YouTube media or actual catalog audio. Recorded start times (30s/42s) do not drive a source cut. Vertex Gemini detector exists only as a returned Python code string: GCS video → suggested 30–60s timestamps + track IDs + audience. No executed SDK dependency/provider call. |
| Docker | Python 3.12 + FFmpeg + fonts, nonroot user; loopback 8080, health check, persistent `/data` SQLite/renders volume. `MARATHON_*` naming retained. Starts with a generated sample clip. Do not operate/restart/delete the existing reference runtime as part of investigation. |
| Container CI | Builds, checks empty-volume startup/dashboard/MP4 bytes and SQLite survival after container replacement. Latest five GitHub runs report failure; latest `38820318167` has no failed step details and its log is unavailable. Do not assume a code failure cause or claim a current reproducibility pass. Owner's prior successful session is separate evidence. |
| [Workbook](https://github.com/ChaiWithJai/defiant-os/blob/5e6b5c3542e9b2bd3d74080fda649abc650b80ec/public/nipsey_hussle_2026_ugc_videos.xlsx) | Three sheets: **Sourced Videos (2026)** (45 data entries plus header/extra row), **Tier & Format Analytics**, **GCP Clipping App Blueprint**. Original URL/channel/date/counts/type/hook/recommended action, tier/format summaries and six proposed pipeline layers. Download is the static original, not a live dashboard export. |
| [Five-page overview](https://github.com/ChaiWithJai/defiant-os/blob/5e6b5c3542e9b2bd3d74080fda649abc650b80ec/docs/defiant-os.pdf) | Artist/catalog intelligence → creative approval → campaign execution/commercial intelligence; proposed Databricks Delta/Unity Catalog data foundation, Gemini evaluation and a proposed compute-credit collaboration. Architecture/partnership requests are proposals, not delivered integrations or awarded credits. |

## The YouTube sourcing strategy to recover

The workbook specifies:

1. **Discovery:** YouTube Data API v3 + scheduled worker; daily searches for Nipsey Hussle, Blacc Sam, Bino Rideaux, Marathon Burger and catalog track titles. Collect new uploads and repeated view observations to identify momentum.
2. **Source access:** partner/first-party upload into GCS, or source playback via embeds; metadata discovery is separate from having a usable source file.
3. **Understanding:** analyze supplied long-form media for useful story/lyric moments and proposed timestamps, explain suggested track matches, retain manager selection. Workbook proposes 30–90sec; reference prompt says 30–60sec while demo rendering is 5–15sec. Resolve this around the desired demo/task rather than blindly copying defaults.
4. **Production:** speaker reframing, captions, real voice/music mix and outro; FFmpeg and possible tracking tools are suggested. Current code implements only generated demonstration media.
5. **Catalog linkage:** identify recording/ISRC and permitted uses. Printed ISRC text does not link official Shorts audio or establish Content ID clearance.
6. **Distribution/measurement:** creator portal, registered uploads, delivery observations and rev-share/paid outcomes. All remain proposed; no BigQuery/Databricks/ad/Content ID connector is wired.

Do not treat workbook counts, tiers, factual assertions, track IDs, ownership or historical rights statuses as verified. Preserve their original provenance and let the user inspect/refresh sources. A single current view count supports neither velocity nor attribution; retain timestamped compatible observations before deriving growth. AI suggestions should explain relevance, not manufacture measured replay/retention or guaranteed virality.

## Current Defiant versus this desired flow

| Capability | Current integrated Defiant | Missing from the desired Nipsey flow |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Research intake | Manual links/excerpts and previewed bounded imports with provenance | Artist/catalog-specific source inbox, direct workbook mapping and repeatable YouTube discovery |
| Exploration | Typed regional/artist/resource graph, ordered routes, annotations, saved views | Operational video queue with creator/track/workstream filtering and source-first playback |
| Planning | Resource feasibility, reports and explicit multi-destination draft brief | Catalog-track entity + source-to-recording match, clipping workstream objectives/budgets and editable segment proposals |
| Production | Existing editorial/native editing and previews | Real source-media cutting, track mix/ducking, captions/reframe and video-specific artifact lineage |
| Results | Saved report/draft context | Time-series source metrics and actual campaign/recording outcome ingestion; historical demo ROAS is not measurement |

## Reuse decision

**Yes: use defiant-os as the experience and domain-fixture base**, preserving the specific Nipsey use case. Reuse the inbox columns, task sequence, workstream structure, source→track relationship and renderer's useful FFmpeg/audio-envelope techniques. Keep the workbook and overview as attributed product input. Retain optional sample mode so a compelling demo is usable before every connector exists.

Adapt into the existing Svelte/Node scoped Defiant workspace and durable store. Do not replace it with the unauthenticated Python server, another identity system, a global seed or a second competing shell. A narrow worker can reuse Python/FFmpeg where justified; choose that boundary only after following a real source through the experience. Databricks, ads, payouts and forecast architecture must not block the first valuable workflow.

Concrete corrections needed when reusing code: `render` currently marks a source whitelisted automatically; local boost computes fictitious delivery then increments attributed catalog streams; replace those transitions with distinct proposed/reviewed/rendered/planned/delivered facts. No rendering action grants permission or places spend. Use stable source IDs rather than display rank; keep samples/measured/imported/derived data distinct. Preserve current org/destination controls without turning this into a general hardening project.

## Current owner clarification: preprocessing first, 45 sources sufficient

The owner confirmed that 45 videos are enough and that missing historical rows must not block delivery. The uploaded workbook was inspected: SHA-256 `0717324f8b82abbd9a42be744a143b6428152d9c77ba2e4058c975d2e33bc9d3`, three sheets, 45 unique video IDs, all 45 matching the existing source pack. Each has a URL, duration, supplied hook and clipping recommendation. No duplicate import or expansion to 100 is required.

Prioritize source preprocessing before final media rendering: selected public YouTube URL → bounded Gemini video analysis → proposed segment in/out timestamps, evidence/context and recording-fit rationale → inspect/edit/save those proposals. The workbook has no exact segment-boundary columns. Gemini/Vertex supports YouTube URL video input; this is video understanding, distinct from Google Search grounding and from the existing YouTube Data API metadata adapter. A local MP4/WAV is not a prerequisite for this preprocessing step. Keep proposed timestamps distinct from observed/reviewed facts, preserve original records and manager notes, and use the existing approved budget/runtime rather than introducing a new paid architecture.

Final MP4 cutting/mixing still requires accessible media bytes; YouTube analysis returns text/structured output, not a downloadable source video. That is a later rendering dependency and must not block URL-based preprocessing. The previous manual-render-first order is superseded by this explicit owner clarification. Do not claim URL analysis, exact timestamps or a successful clip are implemented merely because metadata discovery works.

Official capability reference: https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/samples/googlegenaisdk-textgen-with-youtube-video

## Delivery tasks and acceptance

- [ ] In a dedicated worktree, reproduce/document the reference flow with the workbook and retained source hashes. Record exact reference commit, screenshot each task surface and diagnose container CI only far enough to obtain a reliable isolated preview. No paid calls, existing runtime replacement or volume deletion.
- [x] Deliver the **Nipsey creator-video inbox** inside Defiant: import preview, source links/playback where available, creator/date/counts/observed-at, narrative hook, proposed catalog match, workstream/status filters, source inspection and selected-source URL state. Keep demo labels unobtrusive and truthful. Integrate graph/report navigation as optional context rather than forcing graph traversal before video work.
- [x] Add a bounded YouTube metadata discovery adapter behind the same inbox contract. Save editable query set, run time, canonical video/channel IDs, dedupe, observations, paging/quota/error state. Preserve existing reviewed records on refresh. Establish required credentials/quota/cost before enabling scheduled calls; do not treat current provider specifications as researched by this source audit.
- [ ] One source-to-short vertical slice: approved accessible source file + known permitted audio → suggested/manual timestamps → inspect/adjust → render actual 9:16 cut + mixed audio → play/reopen same artifact. Carry original source and recording references through revisions. URL-based model proposals come first under the owner clarification above; actual cutting/mixing follows when accessible media bytes are available.
- [ ] Carry selected source/segment/track/brief into the existing destination/editor workflow with a report-return path and saved context. Preserve original candidate review/rights facts. No automatic publishing, outreach, ad spend or payout.
- [ ] Evaluate the whole journey for Steve/Carlos: find a useful Nipsey source, explain why it fits a song, select a moment, preview a short and prepare the campaign without reconstructing the brief. Use the original as the side-by-side experience baseline. File only concrete residual API/screen gaps exposed by that journey.

Delivery order: **reference parity and source inbox → live metadata → bounded YouTube preprocessing → inspect/edit/save moments → campaign handoff → actual source clip and complete manager journey**, with demoable increments. The 45-source working set is sufficient. Paid delivery, rights-provider automation, revenue attribution and Databricks integration remain explicit later slices, rather than silent claims in the first demo.

## Investigation limits

Read-only source/history/workbook/PDF/CI inspection on 2026-10-19; no reference app launched, media retrieved, model invoked, ad placed, repository code changed or database migrated. This documents the complete repository inventory and code paths, not a reproduction of the owner's prior successful session or validation of external video facts. Current Defiant delivery comparison uses the merged specification and #209/#211/#214 acceptance records. The Thursday source is the newly identified missing reference and supersedes assumptions that no usable earlier workflow existed.

comments.author: ChaiWithJai
comments.text:
## Reconcile the three inputs: seed, proposed engine and Thursday workflow

The seeded A&R model and defiant-os solve adjacent stages of the same job. Combine them instead of choosing one or treating the regional graph as a substitute for a source inbox.

| Input | Useful base | Missing or unimplemented behavior | Reuse in this ticket |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Original three-part A&R proposal | Discover talent → explore regional opportunity → assemble owned-network partners into a campaign | Claimed automatic YouTube/Gemini discovery, velocity/chemistry scores and audience multipliers were not implemented in the inspected engine; some missing playbooks/rights assumptions | Preserve the product questions and explicit route/partner reasoning. Replace speculative automatic results with source candidates and manager decisions first. |
| Seeded graph + now-delivered Defiant | Six regions, eight corridors, six example artist signals, three cross-region simulations, nine connector examples; plus implemented scoped graph, notes/views, resource feasibility, report snapshots and editor handoff | Example identities, metrics, simulations and relationships do not establish live discoveries or calibrated predictions. No recurring YouTube scouting or actual source-video clipping | Existing graph supplies context after a candidate is selected. Reuse stable IDs, evidence, annotations, resource constraints, reports and destination handoff. Add source/catalog/clip entities without rebuilding these foundations. |
| Thursday defiant-os | 45 Nipsey video rows, 12 catalog tracks, four themed workstreams, source search/filtering, track match and clip setup UI; persisted local actions and generated MP4 demonstration | No live YouTube search/history; source rows and matches are preloaded. No real selected-video cut, catalog audio ingestion, actual ads or measured attribution | Use its inbox and source→song→short sequence as the primary catalog-development workflow. Import its records as an explicitly labeled example research pack; reuse the interaction, not automatic clearance/boost status transitions. |

### Two entry points, one downstream plan

**Catalog-led:** select Nipsey / a recording / a workstream → inspect relevant creator videos and interviews → choose a moment and track → optionally explore a region or collaborator → report/brief → existing campaign editor.

**Talent-led:** choose a region or artist → inspect supporting source videos → compare a route and collaborators → report/brief → existing campaign editor.

The first is the owner's Thursday use case and should lead this ticket. Both share the same evidence/selection/report/campaign spine. Do not force managers through a regional graph before viewing useful videos.

### Seed adaptation: concrete mapping

- Keep the current six-city pack as optional **diasporic talent examples**. Add the Thursday workbook/SQLite constants as a separately named **Nipsey catalog discovery example** pack. Neither silently imports into the two publishing brands, and neither claims live retrieval.
- A `SourceVideo` holds canonical provider/video/channel IDs, URL, title, published date, provenance and evidence references. Map the Thursday video rows here; retain original rank only as an import reference, not durable identity.
- A `SignalObservation` attaches metric/value/unit/observed-at/method to that source. Import workbook counters as historical supplied values with observation time unknown unless established. Do not generate a velocity field from one observation. Later YouTube runs append compatible observations to the same source ID.
- A `Recording` holds catalog ID, proposed/verified ISRC, title and supplied audio/permission references. Thursday's 12 tracks populate example records. Existing A&R catalog connectors may reference recordings or external catalog resources; do not merge them automatically on loose title/name similarity.
- A `SourceRecordingMatch` records source, proposed recording, rationale, optional passage/time range, author/model provenance and review state. This bridges Thursday's `matched_isrc` and the original A&R matching intent without inventing a chemistry percentage. Preserve imported matches as proposals.
- A `Workstream` groups intent, artist/recording, source selections, proposed budget and deliverables. Thursday's four themes provide the example structure; existing report/draft handoff remains the downstream authority rather than creating another campaign system.
- A `ClipProposal` links source, interval, recording/audio asset, crop/caption/mix settings and review state; a `RenderArtifact` records actual inputs, revision and output. The seeded narrative hook is a starting editorial hypothesis, not a verified timestamp. This is the new production slice; the graph need not store media bytes.
- Existing graph region/artist/resource IDs remain context links. Existing shared annotations, path/cluster selection, reports and destination controls are reused, not duplicated into Python/SQLite tables. Note/selection targets need a compatible source/match/clip ID contract.

These are conceptual contracts to fit into the existing bounded store, not a demand for seven new tables or a graph database. Document deviations against the demonstrated UI need.

### Smallest valuable seeded demo

1. Choose the **Nipsey catalog discovery example** pack in the isolated enabled Defiant workspace.
2. Open the familiar video inbox and filter the 'Behind the Bars / lyric lore' workstream. Inspect the supplied Shady Blue / Blue Laces 2 example as a candidate, with source link and provenance visible. Do not endorse the title's factual claims without review.
3. Inspect/edit its proposed track match and write a manager note. Offer the graph only when the user wants route/partner context.
4. Save a report and create a deliberate campaign brief with the existing working handoff. This can be demoed before live sourcing or media cutting is complete.
5. Next replace the example input with one bounded YouTube metadata run using the same source contract; show last checked and new/updated candidates without disturbing prior review.
6. Then add one actual authorized source file/audio pair and an editable timestamp range to prove the real clip path. The original demonstration renderer remains clearly separate until this passes.

This makes the seed a reusable product fixture and acceptance scenario, not a production truth source. It also creates a clean adapter seam: manual import, workbook import and later YouTube discovery all feed the same inbox, evidence inspector and planning flow.

### What specifically remains new

Source-first inbox integrated with Defiant; repeatable reference-pack import and dedupe; catalog recording/match/workstream UI; live metadata collection and observation history; actual media interval editing/rendering. The regional graph, shared notes/views, report snapshots and explicit editor handoff are delivered foundations. Automated talent scoring, growth forecasts, advertising activation and royalty attribution are separate later work and should not gate the Nipsey source-to-campaign demo.

comments.author: gxz321
comments.text:
Hi — I went through Issue #281 and the recent implementation work around #288, #299, #301 and #307.

From what I can see, the creator-video inbox and bounded YouTube metadata workflow are already in place. The main remaining acceptance path appears to be the real authorized source/video + audio workflow: render the actual 9:16 clip, persist and reopen the artifact, carry it through the report/Campaign Studio handoff, and then validate the complete manager journey.

comments.author: ChaiWithJai
